analysis_steps.goal: Compare ALMA dust maps with JWST line positions

method.value: Resample ALMA 315/679 GHz and HST images to a common 10 mas grid and overlay the [Ar VI] and [Ca IV] positions; assess offsets against astrometric uncertainties; show homologous expansion contours

evidence.quote: The dashed black contours in the middle panel of Figure 25 illustrate this effect, assuming homologous expansion from the center

assumptions.value: Homologous expansion over about 3,100 days between the 679 GHz and JWST epochs (~30%)

evidence.quote: during which time the ejecta would have expanded by nearly 30%

validation.value: Offset compared with combined astrometric and statistical uncertainties (3 sigma)

evidence.quote: We find that the offset is within the 3$\sigma$ confidence intervals (but outside the 2$\sigma$ intervals)

used_for.value: Resampling ALMA and HST images to a common pixel grid

results_numeric.quantity: [Ar VI] source offset from ER center (blue interval)

evidence.quote: offsets of ($30\pm 10$ mas south, $63\pm 10$ mas east) for \[-400, -100\] $\rm{km\ s^{-1}}$
The offset and blueshift could imply a kick velocity of $510 \pm 55$ $\rm{km\ s^{-1}}$ for the neutron star.

findings_qualitative.value: The [Ar VI] and [Ca IV] positions lie within the bright 315 GHz dust emission; the 679 GHz dust blob peak is offset NE of [Ar VI] by 2-3 sigma, but the ~10-year expansion prevents firm conclusions.

evidence.quote: Considering these uncertainties, we cannot draw any firm conclusions about the connection between the dust blob and line-emitting region.

claims.hypothesis: Is the ALMA 679 GHz dust blob co-located with the JWST [Ar VI] compact-object source?
claims.experiment: Overlay JWST line positions on ALMA 315 and 679 GHz images accounting for astrometric errors and expansion
claims.result: Blob peak offset NE of [Ar VI] by between 2 and 3 sigma
claims.finding: No firm conclusion about a connection

evidence.quote: though the positions are consistent within the 3$\sigma$ astrometric uncertainties

claims.hypothesis: Do the innermost ejecta lines imply a neutron star kick?
claims.experiment: Combine [Ar VI] offset and Doppler shift
claims.finding: Consistent with a compact object kick, assuming it is near the emitting region

evidence.loc: Position and relation to the neutron star kick velocity
evidence.quote: translating to a 3D kick velocity of $510 \pm 55$ $\rm{km\ s^{-1}}$

limitations_admitted.value: The ~3,100 day gap and ~30% ejecta expansion between ALMA 679 GHz and JWST epochs complicate the comparison; ALMA astrometry is 10-15 mas.

evidence.quote: a major complication in this comparison is that the observations were obtained $\sim 3,100$ days apart
